summary: run_child() doesn't call task.uncancel() after catching CancelledError on Python 3.11+, causing spurious ERROR logs, duplicate commands, and repeated cancellation loops when child workflows are cancelled.
userImpact: Users see spurious ERROR logs when cancelling child workflows on Python 3.11+, duplicate commands sent to the server, and unexpected log noise despite correct execution results.
rootCause: run_child() catches CancelledError without calling task.uncancel(), leaving the cancellation counter at 1. On Python 3.11+, this causes CancelledError to be re-raised on every await, creating a loop that registers multiple callbacks on the result future, generating spurious warnings when the future resolves.
proposedFix: Call task.uncancel() after catching CancelledError to clear the cancellation counter, allowing the loop to wait normally for the result instead of re-raising immediately.
workaround: Install a logging.Filter on 'temporalio.worker._workflow_instance' to suppress ERROR messages matching both 'ChildWorkflowError exception in shielded future' and 'Child Workflow execution cancelled'.
keyQuote: On Python 3.11+, calling handle.cancel() on a running ChildWorkflowHandle causes multiple RequestCancelExternalWorkflow commands to be sent instead of one.
